findings.reason: §7's own done-when item 3 ("No string literal under `reckon/` names a tombstoned verb as a `reckon crew` command; a violation is reported with its module and line") cannot pass while this emitter survives, and the node is fenced out of the file that must change, so either §7's write paths must add `reckon/crew/recovery_classification.py` (and the five-module enumeration must include it) or the folded-verb scan's scope must be narrowed.
findings.text: §7 enumerates five modules that build folded-verb command strings and asserts "That covers reckon's skills, references and agent files, and the command strings five modules build", but `reckon/crew/recovery_classification.py:640` returns the coordinator-facing action string `f"reckon crew repair-status --run {run_id} --status complete …"` in the `exited-unfinished` classification, and `reckon/mcp.py:2148`'s crew-tool docstring still names `crew resume-ready` as a command; `repair-status` and `resume-ready` are both folded by §7, neither file is in §7's write paths, and `recovery_classification.py` appears in no section's write paths at all

findings.reason: a node implementing item 1 literally would tombstone `crew merge` unconditionally and retire a verb that §4's evidence is meant to show is still the form for a head with no run.
findings.text: done-when item 1 asserts "every old invocation in the table except the two deleted names prints its successor through its tombstone", yet §7's mechanism (:206) tombstones `crew merge` only "when §4's evidence counts no merge of a head that no run produced in the last thirty days", and done-when item 4 treats the same tombstone as conditional ("and one fewer again when `crew merge` is tombstoned"), so item 1 requires a tombstone the mechanism may legitimately decline to create

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — every module, test and skill/reference §7 names resolves in the tree (`reckon/crew/claims.py` exposes `narrow_claim`/`release_claim` at :90/:128; the five emitter modules carry the named strings; all eight skill/reference files and `docs/AGENTS.md` exist).
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §7's done-when item 1 asserts "every old invocation in the table except the two deleted names prints its successor through its tombstone", but the §7 mechanism makes `crew merge`'s tombstone conditional on §4's evidence, so the measure demands a tombstone the mechanism may not create.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §7 names no session scratchpad or node-local path; its fixtures and gate live under the repository's usual evidence convention, and no evidence path it names is transient.
rubric_items.naming: pass — no plan label, stage name, ticket number or version tag reaches §7's new filenames or symbols; `tests/test_crew_families_fold.py` and the `crew repair|budget|check` verbs are named by mechanism.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §7's mechanism states its fold "covers ... the command strings five modules build", but at least one live emitter outside those modules and outside §7's write paths still names a folded verb as a `reckon crew` command.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §7 carries one deliverable, folding the §1-table verb families behind flags, and measures it with one gate (`tests/test_crew_families_fold.py`).
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §7's `depends-on` names s6 and s5, both of which exist, and those edges transitively carry s2 (which creates `reckon/crew/tombstones.py`) and s4 (whose merge-count evidence §7 reads); every write-path overlap with a peer section is serialized by a declared edge.
